title: Longest palindromic substring
summary: Stand at every middle of a word and let the echo spread both ways while the letters match; keep the longest echo.
goal: Find the longest stretch of the word that reads the same both ways

mapping.formal: A centre: a letter or a gap between letters

examples.label: racecars
examples.explanation: racecar reads the same both ways; no longer stretch does.

examples.label: cbbd
examples.explanation: The longest echo is centred on the gap between the two b's.

examples.label: One letter
examples.explanation: A single letter is a palindrome.

ladder.name: Check every stretch
ladder.idea: Check every substring, from longest to shortest, for whether it reads the same both ways.

ladder.name: Remember shorter palindromes
ladder.idea: A stretch is a palindrome when its ends match and the stretch inside is one. Fill a table from short stretches to long.
ladder.insight: Checking a stretch repeats the work done for the stretch inside it. Remembering inner answers turns each check into one comparison.

ladder.name: Expand from every centre
ladder.idea: For each centre, a letter or the gap between two letters, widen while both ends match. Keep the longest.
ladder.insight: Every palindrome has a centre, and growing outward from it checks exactly the same pairs as the table, without storing the table.

transfer.problem: Count how many substrings of a word are palindromes.
transfer.explanation: Expand from every centre; each successful widening is one more palindrome.

selfCheck: Tries both odd centres (a letter) and even centres (a gap).
Stops widening at the first mismatch.
